title: When the Silence Wakes
premise: Mara Underhill, a bridge inspector whose marriage to her husband Theo has settled into a silence measured in millimeters, hears a song on the radio that her late brother Danny wrote and never recorded. The song's existence means someone in the old neighborhood circle kept it alive—and kept a secret about the night Danny died that the whole family arranged itself around. As Mara and Theo trace the song through estranged friends and rerouted bus lines back to the neighborhood being demolished, their marriage is forced into its first honest load-bearing conversation in years. The book ends with Mara learning the truth—that Danny's death was an accident Theo witnessed and never confessed—and choosing, with Theo finally speaking, to rebuild rather than collapse.
about_author: Gideon Thackeray is the pen name of a former structural engineer who spent eleven years inspecting bridges across the industrial Midwest before turning to fiction. His work examines how families, like structures, fail slowly and invisibly until they don't.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On a routine bridge inspection, Mara measures tolerances with forensic care while cataloguing everything she and Theo no longer say at home. The chapter establishes her habit of translating emotional distance into engineering language. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Song That Was Never Recorded
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Driving home, a radio DJ plays an obscure local track—Danny's song, note for note, though he never recorded it. Mara sits in the parked car through three rotations of the dial. Emotional beat: the past cracking open like concrete under freeze-thaw.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo notices Mara's distraction but misreads it as an affair, retreating further into his routine. We see his own guilt-tinged avoidance of anything touching Danny's name. Emotional beat: two people inventorying the same marriage from opposite ends.

chapters.title: Rerouted
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara learns the old neighborhood's last bus line will be permanently rerouted next month, and the block where Danny died is slated for demolition. She visits her mother, who shuts the subject down mid-sentence. Emotional beat: urgency hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: People Who Kept It Alive
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the record label credit, Mara finds Wes, Danny's old bandmate, now running a failing guitar shop. Wes confirms someone gave him a home recording after Danny's death—but won't say who, or what else was on the tape. Emotional beat: hope entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback braided with present: the night Danny died, sixteen-year-old Theo saw what happened on the pedestrian walkway and said nothing, letting the family's version stand. Present-day Theo realizes Mara is digging toward exactly that night. Emotional beat: guilt tightening like a cable under load.

chapters.title: The Tape
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wes relents and plays the full cassette: Danny's song, then thirty seconds of recorded argument between Danny and teenage Theo from hours before the fall. Mara hears her husband's young voice saying things she can't unhear. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground of her marriage shifting.

chapters.title: Load Test
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mara confronts Theo; he confesses the accident he witnessed and his decades of silence, including why Danny's death let him become the son their mother needed. The fight is the novel's climax—cruel, precise, and finally honest. Emotional beat: catastrophic failure or first true contact.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara returns to the neighborhood as the old block comes down, meeting her mother there; the two speak plainly about Danny for the first time. Mara decides the secret didn't kill them—silence did. Emotional beat: grief finally given room to move.

chapters.title: Resonance
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, Mara and Theo attend a small memorial concert where Wes plays Danny's song publicly, and the found family of the old neighborhood gathers one last time. Theo speaks Danny's name aloud without flinching. Emotional beat: rebuilt, not restored—a structure that admits its cracks.
